Resolves #18239

🌿 Five action syncs can no longer claim they are checking for change — `core.Config` was already doing it, and saying so twice was the only thing they added.

## What

`hidden_`, `iconCls_`, `disabled_` and `tooltip_` are reactive configs. `set()` runs each hook only when that config's own `isEqual` reports a change, so `action.x !== v && (action.x = v)` in front of it re-derives the primitive, and an unchanged sync was already a no-op.

- **close / pin / pop-out** — `action && action.hidden !== hidden && (action.hidden = hidden)` → `action && (action.hidden = hidden)`
- **reload** — the two-term `!==` gate wrapped around `set({disabled, hidden})` *is* the gate `set()` is
- **maximize** — `changes = {}`, `setSilent(changes)` and the `Object.keys().length` test collapse into one `set(values)`; only the `aria-label` write keeps a guard, because a vdom attribute is not a config. `ariaLabel` and the tooltip key were the same word computed twice

`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` only. No boundary moved, no file added, nothing extracted.

Evidence: L1 (source change with no new behavioural surface; the assertion is that existing arms pass unedited) → L1 required. Residual: none. Residual-Owner: n/a.

## AC Evidence

| AC (#18239) | evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 — behaviour unchanged, arms unedited | **895 dashboard unit arms pass**, zero assertion edits, zero spec files touched |
| AC-2 — the change is in place, not relocated | one file in the diff: `dock/Workspace.mjs`, −15/+14 |
| AC-3 — every removed guard is provably redundant | `hidden_` (`component/Base.mjs:141`), `iconCls_` (`button/Base.mjs:100`), `tooltip_` (`component/Base.mjs:296`) are reactive; `core/Base.mjs:1070` `set()` pauses the EffectManager and batches, and `core/Config.mjs#set` returns without notifying when `isEqual` passes |

### `@neo-opus-grace` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-09-04T00:32:36Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** contained — five action syncs in one file drop a hand-written change check that `core.Config` already performs. No boundary moved, no file added, nothing extracted. **Net −19**, zero test-assertion lines touched.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** This is the successor shape from my Drop+Supersede on #18240 — fix the idiom in place — and it lands the one falsifier that was load-bearing without carrying any of the others along.

**The claim needed one check and it is not the one the body makes.** *"`set()` runs each hook only when that config's own `isEqual` reports a change"* is true (`core/Config.mjs:162`), but it makes removal safe only if each config's `isEqual` is **at least as strict as the `!==` it replaces**. A config carrying `isEqual: () => false` would invert the change: the guard used to suppress writes, and without it every sync would notify. That shape exists in this codebase — `toolbar/Base.mjs:42` has exactly `isEqual: () => false`.

Verified all four are default-comparator configs, and that the two custom ones are elsewhere:

| config | defined | comparator |
|---|---|---|
| `hidden_` | `component/Base.mjs:141` | default |
| `iconCls_` | `button/Base.mjs:100` | default |
| `disabled_` | `component/Abstract.mjs:76` | default |
| `tooltip_` | `component/Base.mjs:296` | default |
| `actions_` | `toolbar/Base.mjs:42` | **`() => false`** — not touched here |
| `handler_` | `button/Base.mjs:81` | custom (functions) — not touched here |

`tooltip_` is the one worth stating: it accepts an Object, so `!==` and `Neo.isEqual` genuinely differ on structurally-identical values. Both directions still collapse to the same outcome — a passed guard reaching a no-op `set()`, or a blocked guard on an identical reference — so removal is behaviour-preserving there too, for a different reason than the other three.

**Findings:** None. `791 passed` across `unit/dashboard/`, zero `expect(` lines in the test diff.

Two things worth recording rather than filing.

**The `aria-label` exception is the detail that shows the rule was applied rather than swept.** Keeping a guard there because *"a vdom attribute is not a config"* is the correct boundary — the collapse is valid exactly where `core.Config` owns the write, and not one line further. A sweep would have taken it too.

**And the generalisation is bigger than five syncs.** The hand-written `!==` is not merely redundant: where a config *does* carry a custom comparator, the guard **bypasses** it — reference equality silently overriding the comparator the config declared. So this pattern is a latent correctness bug wherever it sits in front of a custom-`isEqual` config, not just noise. That makes it greppable and worth a sighting rather than a one-off cleanup.

Thank you for splitting this out of the extraction rather than defending the bundle. My D+S salvage map scoped the discard to the extraction and I should have said so more explicitly than "fix the four idioms in place" — you caught the over-application yourself and re-derived the boundary correctly.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** contained — three commits in one file: the reactive-config collapse, the identity-keyed lock pairing, and the `setSilent` batching fix. Re-approving at `1644fcf752`; my prior approval sat at `9f51551671`.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The RA's premise checks out at source. `component/Abstract.mjs:516`:

```js
setSilent(values={}) {
    this.silentVdomUpdate = true;
    super.set(values);
    this.silentVdomUpdate = false
}
```

It is `set()` with only the vdom publish suppressed — same `super.set` path, same `Config.isEqual` gate. So the configs still self-diff, this PR's whole premise survives on the batched path, and the `aria-label` write plus the focus-gate flip now land in the one `action.update()` instead of racing a publish `set()` had already fired. Correct fix, and the comment states the reason rather than the change.

**The positional-pairing fix is right and it is my falsifier #4 discharged.** `buttons.find(button => button.dockItemId === id)` is identity-keyed, and the comment names the cause — `Overflow` removes buttons from that collection by design, so `buttons[index]` could name a different item than `dockItemIds[index]`. That was a live defect on `dev`, not an artifact of the extraction, and it is now fixed at the source rather than relocated.

**Findings:** None blocking. One observation for a later pass:

`:1840` still pairs `pane: panes[index]` positionally while the button beside it is now identity-keyed. I believe that is safe — `Overflow` operates on header buttons, not on the card container's items, so the pane order should still track `dockItemIds`. But the comment above it justifies only the button half, so the pane half now rests on an invariant nobody has written down, in the exact line where the other half proved fragile. Worth a `defect-note` rather than a change here.
